verdict.rationale: Oneleet documents service keys meant for AI agent automation, MCP servers and scripts. These keys are decoupled from user accounts and scope-limited, which supports headless, non-interactive access. Its Code Security product also provides a CI check that blocks new issues in pull requests. There is no documented CLI, CI runner or pipeline integration guide, and probes found no public OpenAPI spec, so how deeply it can be automated is unproven. Missing for 10: documented CLI or headless runner, CI pipeline integration docs beyond the PR check, a public API reference/OpenAPI spec, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Use **service keys** for AI agent automation, MCP servers, and scripts to interact with your Oneleet workspace. Service keys are decoupled from user accounts and can be scoped for specific tasks.
Grant Full access to all tenant service-key scopes, or choose Limit access to… to grant only specific scopes.
with a CI check that keeps new issues out of your pull requests
